plan.title: Liver treated vs control: descriptive DE, no replicates
plan.analytical_narrative: The data profile shows one treated liver sample and one control liver sample (12000 genes x 2 samples), raw salmon gene counts with zero biological replication. With n=1 per group, no within-group variance can be estimated, so DESeq2 (or any count model) cannot fit a valid dispersion and any p-value it emits has no inferential basis (confirmed by the knowledge service, rule R-0003, and by the knowledge_check gate which forbids an inferential test on this design). The plan therefore runs the standard exploratory/QC steps, computes size-factor-normalized counts and a descriptive (unshrunk) log2 fold change per gene, and stops there for gene-level 'significance' — no p-values, no FDR. To still extract biological direction from the ranked descriptive fold changes, downstream interpretation uses an over-representation analysis (ORA, ranked-list GSEA is explicitly disallowed by the knowledge gate for this no-replicate situation) against MSigDB Hallmark and Reactome gene sets on the genes passing a stated |log2FC| threshold, with the tested-gene universe as background. The final report states every threshold, the complete absence of inferential testing, and what design (biological replicates) would be needed to support a real differential expression test.
